Events can be stored as independently identified records when audit needs require them; this mini fixture has no event table. Payments and refunds also need separate records because each attempt’s amount, target, and outcome matter. Kardinalitas menjawab berapa record dapa: Cardinality asks how many records can be related; optionality asks whether a relationship can be absent. Under this example policy, a student can have zero, one, or many guardians. A guardian can likewise support zero, one, or many students. Ask each direction separately: multiple guardians per student does not itself establish whether one guardian can support siblings. Business requirements define the minimum and maximum rather than whichever table is easiest to edit.
Relasi satu-ke-satu berarti setiap sisi: A one-to-one relationship means at most one counterpart on each side, not necessarily a mandatory counterpart. An optional student profile can use student_id NOT NULL UNIQUE on the profile: every profile references one student and each student has at most one profile. A student without a profile remains possible because a child foreign key does not create a child for every parent. In a one-to-many relationship, the child foreign key is not UNIQUE when a parent may have several children.
Hubungan siswa–wali adalah many-to-many: Student–guardian is a many-to-many or N:M relationship. The lesson_student_guardians junction stores one row per student–guardian pair. Its composite primary key (student_id, guardian_id) prevents recording the same pair twice while allowing one student with different guardians and one guardian with different students. Both columns are foreign keys, requiring valid endpoints for every relationship. PK/FK in the diagram marks that dual role; relationship describes the guardian’s role in the pairing rather than a general attribute of either person.
Memasang UNIQUE pada student_id saja aka: UNIQUE on student_id alone would restrict each student to one guardian. UNIQUE on guardian_id alone would restrict a guardian to one student, preventing siblings from sharing one. Storing IDs as a string also loses foreign-key checking per pair. This example permits one record per pair with one current relationship label. If a pair needs simultaneous roles or validity history, change relationship grain deliberately rather than hiding several facts in one label.
Hubungan opsional tidak berarti endpoint: An optional relationship does not mean NULL endpoints
Elina pada contoh belum mempunyai relasi: Elina has no guardian relationship in this example. Absence is represented by zero junction rows rather than a row with NULL guardian_id. Existing junction rows still require both endpoints. A LEFT JOIN from students retains Elina; COUNT(sg.guardian_id) gives zero because it counts real matches. COUNT(*) would count the outer placeholder row and incorrectly give one. String_agg without guardians is NULL, meaning no list rather than an invented empty guardian name.
Menghapus satu baris junction hanya memu: Deleting one junction row removes one relationship, unlike deleting a guardian identity that may still support other students. The setup uses default foreign-key behavior without CASCADE, rejecting deletion of referenced endpoints. If school policy requires at least one guardian before a student becomes active, these foreign keys and composite PK do not enforce that minimum. Appropriate transition policy and transaction coordination are needed. This example is an isolated TEMP extension of a School Finance subset rather than a source-table change.

Invariant adalah pernyataan yang harus t: An invariant must remain true in every valid state. State what is forbidden and when it is checked rather than only desired column names. These eight exercise rules use School Finance as the business contract. Some have seed constraints; others remain design requirements. Mixing those categories makes a diagram look safer than it is. Sample data that happens to be clean is not evidence that every write path is protected.
I1: nilai invoice wajib terisi dan tidak: I1: invoice amount is required and nonnegative. The seed uses NOT NULL and CHECK amount >= 0, so a zero invoice remains valid. I2: a student may have only one invoice for a given period_month. UNIQUE(student_id, period_month), with both columns non-NULL, enforces that pair; different students may have invoices in the same month. This states one invoice per student per month rather than globally unique months.
I3: setiap payment wajib menunjuk invoic: I3: every payment must reference an existing invoice. NOT NULL and the invoice_id foreign key enforce the endpoint rather than invoice settlement. I4: payment amount is required and strictly positive. CHECK amount > 0 checks one amount; two positive payments can still overpay. I5: payment status must be succeeded, pending, or failed. CHECK and NOT NULL restrict labels rather than proving that a provider actually received money.
I6: payment succeeded harus mempunyai pa: I6: a succeeded payment must have a known paid_at. This is an additional business requirement; the seed allows NULL paid_at for all statuses. A proposed CHECK(status <> 'succeeded' OR paid_at IS NOT NULL) can enforce the per-row rule when status is required. I7: under a no-overpayment policy, succeeded payments per invoice must not exceed its amount. The seed does not enforce that aggregate cap. Validation and recording need atomic coordination so two requests cannot spend the same remainder.
I8: satu callback pembayaran dengan iden: I8: one payment callback with the same business identity may produce only one recording effect. A unique payment_id is insufficient because retries can receive new IDs. The seed lacks stable callback identity, so I8 violations cannot be counted from available columns. A design needs an appropriately scoped business key, uniqueness enforcement, and effects recorded in a consistent transaction. An absent identifying column is not proof that duplicate callbacks do not exist.

Siswa–wali · N:M melalui junction UML/ER: Students–guardians · N:M through a UML/ERD junction
PK = identitas unik; FK = referensi waji: PK = unique identity; FK = required reference; 1 = exactly one; 0..N = zero or many. Every column is required except paid_at. Repeated tables represent the same entity rather than duplicate data. Lines show relationships rather than process order; refund limits and lifecycle are not fully constraint-enforced.
Dua kolom PK/FK bersama-sama membentuk s: The two PK/FK columns jointly form one composite pair primary key. Each relationship requires a student and a guardian, while a student or guardian may have no relationship. All columns are required. The junction is repeated to show both foreign keys; it remains one table rather than two copies.
Satu order memiliki 0..N item. Setiap it: One order has 0..N items. Each item must reference exactly one order; an FK does not enforce at least one item when confirmed.
Satu order memiliki 0..N percobaan payme: One order has 0..N payment attempts. Each payment must reference exactly one order; a failed attempt retains its own identity.
Satu payment memiliki 0..N refund. Setia: One payment has 0..N refunds. Each refund must reference exactly one payment; this FK does not require payment success or cap total refunds.
Satu siswa memiliki 0..N baris hubungan: One student has 0..N guardian relationship rows. Each junction row must reference exactly one student.
Satu wali memiliki 0..N baris hubungan s: One guardian has 0..N student relationship rows. Each junction row must reference exactly one guardian; these two 1:N relationships form student–guardian N:M.
